<a id="symbol-PortableRelativePath"></a>
## `PortableRelativePath` · immutable record · [source](paths.aug#L10)

Lexical portable relative path. This value grants no filesystem access or containment guarantee.

It takes `text` as a string, kept read-only (1 to 1024 ASCII bytes in 1 to 64 slash-separated segments of 1 to 255 bytes.
Segments use letters, digits, period, underscore or hyphen. Empty/dot/dot-dot segments, trailing periods and Windows device basenames are rejected).

Construction can fail with `ConversionError`.

<a id="symbol-PortableRelativePath.initialize"></a>
### `PortableRelativePath.initialize` · [source](paths.aug#L10)

It calls [`_validatePortablePath`](paths.aug.md#symbol-_validatePortablePath) with `text`. [source](paths.aug#L12)

<a id="symbol-joinPortablePaths"></a>
## `joinPortablePaths` · [source](paths.aug#L27)

Join two validated paths with one slash and revalidate all byte, segment and name limits. It takes `left` and `right` as [`PortableRelativePath`](paths.aug.md#symbol-PortableRelativePath). It returns a [`PortableRelativePath`](paths.aug.md#symbol-PortableRelativePath) with `text` from the text `{left.text}/{right.text}`. [source](paths.aug#L28)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
joinPortablePaths(PortableRelativePath left, PortableRelativePath right) returns PortableRelativePath unless ConversionError
```

It takes `left` and `right` as [`PortableRelativePath`](paths.aug.md#symbol-PortableRelativePath). Failures can raise `ConversionError` (The combined path exceeds the supported bounds).

</details>

<a id="symbol-_validatePortablePath"></a>
## `_validatePortablePath` · [source](paths.aug#L30)

It is private to its defining scope. It takes `text` as a string.

It checks that `text.byteLength` does not equal `0` and `text.byteLength` is at most `1024`. It raises a `ConversionError` at the first failed check. It sets `segments` to `text.split` with `separator` `"/"`. [source](paths.aug#L31-L33)

It checks that the number of elements in `segments` is at most `64`. It raises a `ConversionError` at the first failed check. For each `segment` in a snapshot of `segments`, it checks that `segment.byteLength` does not equal `0` and `segment.byteLength` is at most `255` and `segment` does not equal `"."` and `segment` does not equal `".."` and `segment.endsWith` with `suffix` `"."` returns false. It raises a `ConversionError` at the first failed check. [source](paths.aug#L34-L51)

It sets `bytes` to the UTF-8 bytes of `segment`. It sets `index` to `0`. While `index` is less than `segment.byteLength`, it sets `character` to [`asciiAt`](ascii.aug.md#symbol-asciiAt) with `input` from `bytes` and `index`. [source](paths.aug#L39-L45)

It checks that [`asciiLetter`](ascii.aug.md#symbol-asciiLetter) with `character` returns true or `character.isDecimal` returns true or `character` equals `"."` or `character` equals `"_"` or `character` equals `"-"`. It raises a `ConversionError` at the first failed check. It increases `index` by `1`. After the loop, it sets `basename` to [`asciiLower`](ascii.aug.md#symbol-asciiLower) with `text` from the item at index `0` in `segment.split` with `separator` `"."`. [source](paths.aug#L43-L51)

It checks that [`_reserved`](paths.aug.md#symbol-_reserved) with `basename` returns false. It raises a `ConversionError` at the first failed check. If this work raises `IndexError`, it raises a `ConversionError`. [source](paths.aug#L48-L51)

<details>
<summary>Checked interface</summary>

```text
_validatePortablePath(string text) returns void unless ConversionError
```

It takes `text` as a string. Failures can raise `ConversionError`.

</details>

## `_reserved` · [source](paths.aug#L53)

It is private to its defining scope. It takes `basename` as a string. [source](paths.aug#L54-L77)

## Dependencies

It uses [`asciiAt`](ascii.aug.md#symbol-asciiAt), [`asciiLetter`](ascii.aug.md#symbol-asciiLetter), and [`asciiLower`](ascii.aug.md#symbol-asciiLower) from `ascii`.

Built-in operations follow the [language reference](https://greenpandastudios.github.io/augscript/language-constructs).
